data.title: Fox Closes $22 Billion Deal to Buy Roku to Expand Streaming Reach past 100 Million Homes
data.description:
Fox (FOX) finished its $22 billion purchase of Roku (ROKU) on Friday, creating a television giant that pairs live broadcast networks with a leading connected TV platform. Fox Class A shares rose 1.83% to $66.43 on Friday, while Roku shares closed at $160.30.

First announced in June, the deal gives Fox direct access to more than 100 million households that use Roku devices and smart TVs. Combining Fox's live sports and news with Roku's software will help the cable-reliant broadcaster grow its online audience and better target digital ads.

"The closing of this acquisition advances the long-term strategy of FOX," Fox Chief Executive Officer Lachlan Murdoch said in a statement. "Beginning today, our top priority for the combined company is to continue to relentlessly serve audiences and partners, while reinforcing the openness and choice that is the essence of the Roku platform."

Fox Pays Cash and Stock while Targeting $400 Million in Cost Savings

Under the merger terms, Roku investors receive $95.30 in cash and 0.9799 shares of Fox Class A common stock for each Roku Class A and Class B share they owned before closing, according to a company filing. Following the buyout, former Roku stockholders own roughly 26% of Fox's outstanding shares, while existing Fox investors keep the remaining 74%.

Fox expects the tie-up to deliver about $400 million in annual cost savings within two years of closing. Management also projects that the deal will add to free cash flow per share by the second full year. Allen & Company LLC and Morgan Stanley (MS) acted as financial advisors to Fox, while Qatalyst Partners advised Roku.

Anthony Wood Joins Fox Board to Co-Chair Digital Unit

Roku founder Anthony Wood is joining Fox's board of directors and will serve as co-chair of a new division called Fox Digital Platforms. Wood will lead the unit alongside Paul Cheesbrough, who becomes co-chair and CEO of the division.

Fox Digital Platforms brings together Roku, the free ad-supported Tubi streaming service, the Fox One streaming platform, and podcast producer Red Seat Ventures. Fox launched Fox One and bought Red Seat Ventures in 2025 as part of an ongoing push beyond traditional cable television.

"We started Roku more than two decades ago to give people a better way to watch TV, and that mission doesn't change today," Wood said in a statement. "FOX has a deep respect for Roku's culture and wholly shares our commitment to staying open to every content partner."

Is FOX a Good Stock to Buy?

Turning to the Street, FOX stock carries a Moderate Buy consensus based on two Buys and one Hold rating assigned in the past three months. The average 12-month FOX stock price target is $90, which implies 52% upside from the current price. (See FOX stock forecast)
data.author: Annika Masrani

data.title: Tesla (TSLA) Merger with SpaceX Thrown Into Doubt After Midterm Elections, Says Dan Ives
data.description:
Closely followed technology analyst Dan Ives says that a potential merger of Tesla (TSLA) and SpaceX (SPCX) has been thrown into doubt following the U.S. midterm congressional elections. Ives says that Democrats who now control both the U.S. House of Representatives and Senate are likely to make any merger between Elon Musk's two publicly traded companies difficult.

"We will believe a SpaceX/Tesla merger ​happens but ⁠now faces a much tougher regulatory roadmap to get this deal done in 2027 given this new political blue roadmap in DC/Texas," said Ives, who is a partner and senior managing director ⁠at Yorkville ​Ives & Co. Musk said on SpaceX's third-quarter earnings call in October that a merger with Tesla would be a "good idea" and that special committees at the two ​companies were exploring a potential deal.

Tesla's key performance indicators. Source: TipRanks

The Midterm Results

Doubts about a Tesla-SpaceX merger are growing after Republican lawmakers suffered a resounding defeat in the midterms. With most ballots counted, the Democrats hold 54 seats in the U.S. Senate versus 44 seats for the Republican Party. In the House of Representatives, the Democrats are on track to win more than 250 seats, there best showing since 2008.

The Democrats will now be able to put a check on the policies of Republican President Donald Trump, who's tariffs and war in Iran have proved deeply unpopular with the electorate. They are also expected to be less pro-business and could also kibosh corporate mergers and put a moratorium on the artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure buildout, both of which would impact Musk's businesses.

Tesla Cancels the Cybertruck

Ives comments on the SpaceX merger come on the same day that Tesla announced it is ending production of its Cybertruck. Musk announced on social media that the company will end Cybertruck production at its Texas manufacturing facility by the middle of 2027. The Cybertruck is being discontinued so that Tesla can make room for increased production of its self-driving Cybercab.

Tesla sold fewer than 100,000 Cybertrucks in the U.S. through September of this year, and sales in 2025 declined 48% year-over-year to 20,237 vehicles. The futuristic looking Cybertruck proved polarizing with consumers, with people either loving or hating the vehicle's appearance. The Cybertruck was unveiled in 2019. Tesla initially projected that it would sell 250,000 Cybertrucks a year, but actual sales were much lower than that figure.

Is TSLA Stock a Buy?

Tesla stock has a consensus Moderate Buy rating among 27 Wall Street analysts. That rating is based on 14 Buy, 11 Hold, and two Sell recommendations issued in the last three months. The average TSLA price target of $402.47 implies 4% upside from current levels.
data.author: Joel Baglole

data.title: Why Is the Stock Market Up Today, 11/6/26?
data.description:
Both the S&P 500 (SPX) and the Nasdaq 100 (NDX) are trading higher on Friday with gains of 0.92% and 1.88%, respectively. The gains come after both indexes plunged on Thursday, suffering their steepest single-day declines since the April 2025 tariff crash.

Earlier this week, Gina Hinojosa beat Greg Abbott to become Texas' first Democratic governor since 1995. That sparked concerns of a slowdown in AI growth, as the Democrats have called for stricter regulations on AI and data center development. In addition, Texas accounts for nearly 30% of planned U.S. data center capacity. However, Hinojosa told CNN that she won't ban new data centers in Texas.

AI Stocks Recover as Labor Market Shows Strength

Instead, she wants to ensure that data center companies listen to local residents and address their concerns before building new facilities. "It is not that I hate data centers," she said. "I hate the way they are taking advantage of Texas and that stops when I'm governor." Hinojosa's comments helped drive a rebound in AI stocks, including Nvidia (NVDA), AMD (AMD), and Intel (INTC).

Elsewhere, an upbeat jobs report has also lifted sentiment. In October, nonfarm payrolls rose by 165,000, well above the 70,000 estimate. August's job gains were also revised up to 186,000 from 133,000, while September's were revised up to 60,000 from 29,000.

data.title: Dan Ives Calls Tech Rout a "Golden Buying Opportunity"
data.description:
Wall Street analyst Dan Ives said that Thursday's 5.5% plunge in the Nasdaq Composite created a "golden buying opportunity" in AI stocks after Democrats swept the November 3 midterm elections. The index suffered its worst day since April 2025 and entered correction territory, down nearly 12% from its October 6 record.

Ives compared the selloff with the market drops during the COVID-19 outbreak in March 2020 and the tariff shock in April 2025. He believes that investors are pricing in an end to the U.S. AI infrastructure expansion, even though he expects construction to continue at a slower pace.

For context, Texas Governor-elect Gina Hinojosa wants to temporarily stop new projects until stricter rules are introduced. UBS analysts estimate that restrictions like these could affect about 30% of the new U.S. data center capacity planned for 2028.

However, this does not mean that those projects have been canceled. Instead, some could face construction delays or have trouble getting the approvals they need.

Why Ives Still Expects Heavy AI Spending

Ives now expects growth in AI infrastructure spending to peak in 2027 instead of 2028 or 2029. Even with that earlier peak, he forecasts $3 trillion to $4 trillion of AI-related investment over the next several years. He also believes that major technology companies will spend more than $1 trillion on AI in 2027 alone.

Recent company results help explain his forecast. E-commerce and cloud giant Amazon (AMZN) expects approximately $220 billion in total cash capital spending this year, although that includes investments outside of AI. Software giant Microsoft (MSFT) reported $45.2 billion in capital expenditures in its latest quarter, while revenue from its Azure cloud business grew by 48%.

However, Microsoft also reported delays in receiving computing capacity from outside suppliers. That shows why strong demand alone cannot guarantee that construction will stay on schedule.

Ives argues that projects with permits already in place should keep moving forward, and expects most facilities planned for the next 18 months to be built.

Is QQQ ETF a Buy, Sell, or Hold?

Turning to Wall Street, analysts have a Strong Buy consensus rating on the Invesco QQQ Trust (QQQ), which tracks the tech-heavy Nasdaq 100. This is based on 89 Buys, 12 Holds, and zero Sells assigned in the past three months, as indicated by the graphic below. Furthermore, the average QQQ price target of $983.96 per share implies 49.6% upside potential. (See QQQ Stock Forecast).

data.title: S&P 500 Rebounds After Worst Selloff Since April 2025 as AI Stocks Rally
data.description:
The S&P 500 (SPX) is up 0.97% on Friday following a brutal trading session the previous day that saw the benchmark index plunge 4.4%, its worst day since the April 2025 tariff crash. Fears of slowing data center development from a Democrat-controlled Congress contributed to the decline, although comments from Texas' governor-elect have helped ease those concerns.

Gina Hinojosa, who beat Greg Abbott to become Texas' first Democrat governor since 1995, said she doesn't hate data centers. Instead, she believes that some companies who build data centers have taken advantage of Texans by building them in their communities without properly listening to residents or considering how these projects affect them. Nearly 30% of planned U.S. data center capacity is located in Texas.

"It is not that I hate data centers," she told CNN. "I hate the way they are taking advantage of Texas and that stops when I'm governor."

AI Rebound, Jobs Report Drive S&P 500 Higher

Hinojosa added that a strong AI industry in Texas and protections for its people are not mutually exclusive. Furthermore, communities should have a say in where data centers are built and how these projects affect their neighborhoods, she said. Her comments helped drive a rebound in AI stocks, with Nvidia (NVDA), AMD (AMD), and Intel (INTC) posting notable gains.

Elsewhere, a better-than-expected jobs report is also driving the S&P 500 higher. Nonfarm payrolls increased by 165,000, shattering expectations of 70,000. On top of that, August's payroll growth was revised up to 186,000 from 133,000, while September's was raised to 60,000 from 29,000.

In addition, the unemployment rate fell to 4.1% from 4.2%, below the estimate of 4.2%. The rate has trended between 4.1% and 4.3% since March.

Should You Buy the S&P 500?

Wall Street is bullish on the S&P 500 ETF (SPY). During the past three months, analysts have issued an average SPY price target of $987.88, implying upside of 33.43% from current prices. The 503 holdings in SPY carry 414 buy ratings, 83 hold ratings, and six sell ratings, reflecting strong overall sentiment across the index. The highest price target is at $1,220.09, while the lowest sits at $765.16.

data.title: Bitcoin (BTC) Looks for Direction After Market Selloff
data.description:
Bitcoin (BTC) and other cryptocurrencies are looking for direction after being dragged lower in a broad-based market selloff. Bitcoin is trading sideways at $75,000 on Nov. 6, near its lowest level in three months. Ethereum (ETH) is trading at $2,200 after digital assets were pulled down alongside equities in a major market selloff.

Every corner of the U.S. market plunged on Nov. 5 as investors grow increasingly worried about the sustainability of the artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure buildout. The blue-chip Dow Jones Industrial Average fell more than 1,800 points on the day and the technology-laden Nasdaq Composite index dropped 5.5%. Since Oct. 1, the Nasdaq has fallen 10% and entered a correction.

Bad News Piles Up for Crypto

The market meltdown has exerted downward pressure on digital assets that were already reeling from the $6.3 billion theft at crypto exchange Binance. At the same time, the future of the Clarity Act legislation has been thrown into doubt after the left-leaning Democratic Party won control of the U.S. Congress in the midterm elections.

The Clarity Act seeks to provide a regulatory framework for cryptocurrencies such as Bitcoin and is seen as key to the future evolution of digital assets. However, many analysts say that new, tougher legislation will likely be needed now with the Democrats in control. The Binance hack and fate of the Clarity Act is negatively impacting sentiment towards cryptocurrencies, say analysts.

Bitcoin ETF Withdrawals

Exchange-traded funds (ETFs) that track the spot price of Bitcoin experienced $430 million U.S. of outflows on Nov. 5 as equity markets melted down. The heavy outflows were led by leading Bitcoin ETFs managed by Fidelity Investments and BlackRock (BLK). Investors pulled money from the ETFs as Bitcoin's price fell more than 5% on the day.

In the week ended Nov. 5, about a dozen U.S.-listed Bitcoin ETFs saw cumulative outflows of $869.8 million. Many investors, particularly large institutions such as hedge funds, began pulling money from Bitcoin ETFs after the Binance hack was disclosed. Some analysts say they expect the outflows from Bitcoin ETFs to continue in the near-term as market volatility persists.
data.author: Joel Baglole

data.title: Dow Jones Shrugs Off Optimistic Jobs Report
data.description:
The Dow Jones (DJIA) is down 0.66% on Friday, despite a better-than-expected jobs report from the Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS). In October, nonfarm payrolls increased by 165,000, well above the estimate of 70,000. The professional and business services sector led the way with 70,000 new payrolls, followed by healthcare at 42,000.

In addition, August's payroll additions were revised higher to 186,000 from 133,000, while September's figure rose to 60,000 from 29,000. "The US economy is averaging nearly +86,000 job gains a month in 2026," said Navy Federal Credit Union Chief Economist Heather Long. "That's much better than the anemic +10,000 average in 2025."

December Rate Hike Bets Rise After Jobs Report

Meanwhile, the unemployment rate edged lower to 4.1% from 4.2%, below expectations of 4.2%. The rate has drifted between 4.1% and 4.3% since March.

Following the report, the odds of a 25-basis-point hike at the December 9 Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting rose to 79.4% from 66.9% a day ago, according to the CME FedWatch tool. With a steady labor market, the Fed has less reason to lower rates and stimulate employment. That comes as inflation has remained above the Fed's 2% target for over five years.

In fact, inflation has erased all wage gains for seven consecutive months, underscoring the severity of rising prices. Over the past year, wages have risen by an average 3.1%, below the average inflation gain of about 3.5%.

Elsewhere, some AI stocks are staging a recovery after the Dow Jones plunged 3.4% on Thursday. Nvidia (NVDA) is up by about 5%, while Caterpillar (CAT), which is closely tied to the data center buildout, is up by over 3%.

Should You Buy the Dow Jones?

Wall Street is bullish on the SPDR Dow Jones Industrial Average ETF (DIA). During the past three months, analysts have issued an average DIA price target of $601.12, implying upside of 16.89% from current prices. The 30 holdings in DIA carry 28 buy ratings, two hold ratings, and zero sell ratings, reflecting strong overall sentiment across the index. The highest price target is at $711.10, while the lowest sits at $490.33.

data.title: Nvidia vs. AMD: Jim Cramer Calls One AI Chip Stock a Bargain, Says the Other Is 'Awfully High'
data.description:
Friday morning is bringing some much-needed relief to semiconductor investors, with Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA) climbing about 4% in early trading and Advanced Micro Devices (NASDAQ:AMD) jumping 8.5%. Both chipmakers are recovering from Thursday's brutal market selloff, which sent Nvidia tumbling 9% and AMD plunging 17%, leaving investors wondering whether the latest rebound marks a buying opportunity or merely a temporary escape from further losses.

The selloff came as Wall Street grew concerned about the sustainability of massive AI infrastructure spending, particularly with political opposition threatening additional data-center construction. AMD also faced heightened scrutiny following its latest earnings report, as investors weighed the company's enormous growth opportunities against a valuation that already assumes considerable future success.

For CNBC's Mad Money host Jim Cramer, however, the two chip giants aren't equally appealing at their current prices. While he believes Nvidia's valuation has become a "bargain," AMD's share price still looks "awfully high" despite its outstanding quarterly performance.

But does Wall Street agree with Cramer's assessment?

Nvidia: A Bargain, but Not Without Risks

Nvidia's latest retreat has created a valuation that Cramer finds attractive, especially considering the company's expected earnings growth. His argument rests on the possibility that demand for AI computing will remain strong enough to support another year of solid financial performance.

"If you think, for example, that Nvidia is going to have a good year in 2027 and just meet the current estimates set out for the company, then you'd have a stock with a growth rate of 70% that's selling for less than 12 times next year's earnings," Cramer explained.

He went further, describing that combination as an "incredible, ridiculous bargain," before reiterating his belief that Nvidia's relatively low earnings multiple could eventually reward investors.

There is, however, an important condition attached to his enthusiasm. Cramer warned that the valuation would lose much of its appeal if restrictions on additional U.S. data centers prevented Nvidia from maintaining its growth trajectory beyond 2027.

That concern has become particularly relevant following the Democrats' midterm election victory, which has raised the prospect of tougher permitting requirements for energy-intensive computing facilities. Nvidia's customers continue investing heavily in AI infrastructure, but delays in building the facilities needed to house its chips could eventually affect demand.

Despite those risks, analysts remain unanimously bullish on Nvidia, awarding the stock a Strong Buy consensus rating based on 33 Buys, zero Holds, and zero Sells. The average 12-month price target stands at $322.50, implying about 71% upside from current levels. (See NVDA stock forecast)

AMD: Outstanding Earnings, But Is the Price Too High?

AMD presents Cramer with a more complicated decision, largely because the company's financial performance has been very strong while its share price has already reflected considerable expectations.

"Perhaps the toughest to analyze is the stock of AMD," Cramer acknowledged, describing its latest quarterly results as among the best he had ever seen.

The chipmaker's long-term opportunity also remains enormous. During his interview with CEO Lisa Su, Cramer heard her reiterate expectations for a $1 trillion addressable market in data centers, illustrating the potential scale of demand for AMD's processors and AI accelerators.

Yet, the veteran commentator isn't convinced that impressive growth prospects automatically justify paying any price for the shares.

"The stock was at $188 in March. By that token, $404 seems awfully high to me. Maybe that's the real problem," Cramer remarked.

Thursday's 17% plunge demonstrated how vulnerable expensive growth stocks can become when investors begin reconsidering their assumptions about future earnings. Friday's 8% rebound suggests buyers are returning, although AMD still faces the challenge of translating its enormous addressable market into profits sufficient to justify its share price.

Wall Street appears more enthusiastic about AMD's prospects than Cramer's cautious remarks might suggest. The stock carries a Strong Buy consensus rating based on 26 Buys and 4 Holds, with no Sell recommendations among the 30 analysts covering the company. The average 12-month price target of $653.50 implies ~49% upside from current levels. (See AMD stock forecast)

Disclaimer: The opinions attributed to Jim Cramer are his own. This article is intended for informational purposes only and does not constitute investment advice. Investors should conduct their own research before making investment decisions.

data.title: RKLB vs. ASTS: One Space Stock Offers 160%+ Upside Ahead of November 9 Earnings
data.description:
Space stocks Rocket Lab (RKLB) and AST SpaceMobile (ASTS) are set to report their Q3 2026 results on November 9 after market close, with investors watching for updates on launch activity and satellite deployment plans. According to TipRanks data, Rocket Lab has a Strong Buy consensus rating, while AST SpaceMobile has a Moderate Buy rating. However, ASTS offers greater upside potential of 167.26%, based on average analyst price targets, compared with 115.67% for RKLB.

RKLB and ASTS Stock Price Performances

Rocket Lab stock rose over 5% in Friday's pre-market trading. However, shares remain down 25% year to date, weighed by delays to its Neutron rocket launch. The shift to 2027 has raised concerns about delayed revenue and higher costs.

Similarly, ASTS stock also inched higher in Friday's pre-market trading, though shares are down 51% year to date. Delays in satellite deployment and rising funding needs have weighed on the stock. The loss of BlueBird 7 and high cash burn have added pressure, while share sales raised dilution concerns. Growing competition from SpaceX's Starlink has also clouded its growth outlook.

Is Rocket Lab Stock a Buy Ahead of Earnings?

Wall Street expects Rocket Lab to report a Q3 loss of $0.07 per share, compared to a loss of $0.03 a year ago. Revenue is expected to grow 65% year-over-year to $257.2 million.  Rocket Lab's Q2 revenue rose 62% to $234 million, while its backlog hit a record $2.36 billion.

This week, Cantor Fitzgerald analyst Andres Sheppard  reiterated an Overweight rating on Rocket Lab with a $122 price target. He cited the company's successful 98th Electron mission and progress on Neutron. Rocket Lab launched three satellites for HawkEye 360 on October 23, bringing its total successful Electron and Haste launches to 98. Cantor expects Neutron's first launch in Q2 2027.

Meanwhile, Citizens analyst Trevor Walsh reiterated a Market Outperform rating but lowered his price target to $90 from $130. He pushed his Neutron launch forecast to late Q2 2027 after defects were found in a first-stage tank component. Walsh views the delay as a timing setback rather than a change to his investment thesis. He also sees continued Electron demand and the pending Iridium (IRDM) acquisition as positives for Rocket Lab.

Overall, Wall Street has a Strong Buy consensus rating on Rocket Lab stock based on 15 Buys and three Holds. The average RKLB stock price target of $99.19 indicates 115.67% upside potential.

Is ASTS a Good Stock to Buy Now?

For Q3 2026, Wall Street expects ASTS to report a loss of $0.42 per share, compared with a loss of $0.77 in Q2. Revenue is forecast at $45.73 million, up from $31.52 million in the prior quarter. Investors will watch for updates on satellite deployment and the company's plans for commercial service.

On October 23, Scotiabank analyst Andres Coello upgraded AST SpaceMobile to Buy from Hold. The 5-star analyst raised his price target to $55.70 from $50.80. Coello said the sell-off following SpaceX's spectrum acquisition was justified. He believes Starlink's new satellites could narrow ASTS's technical lead. However, SpaceX's broader ambitions could also make ASTS more valuable to telecom operators seeking satellite capacity.

Coello sees satellite launch capacity as the main factor for ASTS. Investors remain concerned about delays in getting Bluebird satellites into orbit. However, he expects competing rocket providers to expand launch capacity over the coming months. Scotiabank expects ASTS to achieve continuous commercial service in developed markets by Q4 2027.

Meanwhile, Piper Sandler analyst Alexander Potter downgraded his rating from Buy to Hold and lowered the price target to $54 from $98. The 5-star analyst cited "lower conviction in the pace of satellite launches in 2026-2027." He also warned that SpaceX's push into the direct-to-cell (D2C) market could limit launch availability for ASTS and add to pricing pressure.

Overall, Wall Street has a Moderate Buy consensus rating on AST SpaceMobile stock based on six Buys and five Holds. The average ASTS stock price target of $80.71 indicates 167.26% upside potential.
